correctness.rationale: The mixed-face restrictions yield the exhaustive facet cover Δ(A), Δ(B), and Q_ij tetrahedra; for n>=3 each nonempty intersection of cover members is a simplex with a canonical stabilizer-fixed barycenter. The nerve is ΣL_n where L_n is covered by simplices T_i on incident pair-symbols; their intersections are individual vertices, giving the graph K_n as the second equivariant nerve. The finite-group-equivariant nerve criterion is satisfied by all invariant intersections, so |Ind_2(C_n)| ≃_G Σ|K_n| with side-swap interchanging suspension cones. Thus G-quotient is a cone and contractible. H_1(K_n;Z)=ker[Λ²Z^n→U_n]=Λ²U_n, and side-swap reverses suspension orientation, giving ε over Z. At n=4 the tetrahedral facet cover is pure 3D with nonzero H_2 and cannot be pure shellable. Independently enumerated all actual faces vs facets and computed binary Betti ranks n=3,4,5 as 1,3,6 in H_2; all 12,48,240 S_n×C2 oriented Lefschetz traces matched (-1)^e[((f-1)(f-2))/2 - t]. These finite tests only corroborate the universal equivariant nerve argument.
